# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. Your `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay out, and the pages are built in the browser, so crawlers see an empty page. The only unknown is the canonical address (GEO-015), because no site domain is declared anywhere. The cap of 40 for a blocker applied (GEO-009), but the score is already below it. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking every crawler in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks Googlebot, Bingbot and AI search crawlers not to read any page, so nothing else you fix will be seen. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59. This fixes GEO-009 and GEO-014. It assumes you want to be found. If the block is deliberate, for example on a staging site, tell me and I'll adjust the report. ### 2. Put the page content in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** The server sends an empty `
` and the text only appears after JavaScript runs. Many crawlers and AI tools don't run it, so they see no mugs. The catalogue list is also fetched in the browser. - **Where:** `index.html:8`, `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs')` - **Size:** Large (prerender or server-render, for example with a framework or a prerender plugin) - **Score after this:** +3 points on both ends, on top of item 1 (53–62). ### 3. Give pages a real title, description and language - **Why it matters:** Every page currently shares the title "Vite App", has no description, and `` has no `lang`. Search results and AI tools can't tell what the site is. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small (per-page titles need a head helper such as react-helmet or React 19's `` and `<meta>` tags) - **Score after this:** +2 points on both ends, on top of item 1 (52–61). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, 2 valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed in | Problem | `public/robots.txt:2`, site-wide block | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks Googlebot and Bingbot on both routes. No noindex found | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Can't tell | No canonical, and no site domain declared | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | `index.html:8`, client-only app, no prerendering | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD (structured data) is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is listed | Problem | No sitemap, and no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `index.html:2,5`, both routes share the default title, with no description or `lang` | | GEO-016 | Key pages are reachable through real links | Problem | `src/main.jsx:11`, `/catalogue` only via a button | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Problem | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`, image with no `alt` (Home fails, Catalogue is clear) | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | None present, never scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | None present, never scored | ## Other problems found - **Hero image and Catalogue button have no real link:** `src/main.jsx:11`: `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>Catalogue</button>`. Use `<Link to="/catalogue">`. This is the same fix as GEO-016. ## Worth considering - **Describe the hero image:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: `<img src="/hero.jpg" />`. Add `alt` text saying what the picture shows, and consider `width` and `height`. - **Give each mug its own page:** `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`: `{items.map((m) => <p key={m.id}>{m.name}</p>)}`. Add routes like `/catalogue/:id` with links, so each mug has its own address and can be found separately. - **Show more than a name per mug:** Same line. Price, material and size are not shown as text. Adding them, with Product structured data, might help machines understand the listing. - **Back up the home page claim:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` Add a page covering shipping, contact details and who makes the mugs, and link to it from the navigation. - **Add head basics:** `index.html:4-5` has a charset but no `viewport`, no description and no social tags (`og:title`, `og:image`). - **Say who the site is:** Nothing states the shop's name in machine-readable form. Organization or WebSite structured data with the name and link might help. - **Declare the site's domain:** No domain appears in the repository. Settle it once and use it for canonical tags and the sitemap. - **Add a footer or fuller navigation:** The two pages link only through the one nav. Links onward from the home page to the mug pages would help visitors and crawlers. - **Add a `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** Once a sitemap exists, include real dates. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015:** No canonical tag and no declared domain. Tell me your site's domain, and this becomes a Problem or Clear. - **Bot protection:** Code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Mug data:** The catalogue comes from `/api/mugs`, which isn't in this repository, so I can't judge its content. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find this site, so the blanket `Disallow: /` is treated as a mistake. - The only two routes are `/` and `/catalogue`, taken from `src/main.jsx`. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
